request_context: A request to plan a team sprint in a work-management tool: choosing a project, creating and sizing tasks, tracking how much work fits the team's capacity, and moving unfinished work into the next sprint.

rules.source_quote: If the call fails or the capability is not found, STOP and inform the user
rules.outcome: When the connection to the work-management tool cannot be verified, the answer stops, tells the user the integration is not set up and points them to setup instructions, rather than pretending to plan or create tasks.
rules.why: Continuing without a working connection produces fabricated plans or failed writes the user believes succeeded.
rules.scenario_hint: User asks to plan a sprint but the tool integration is unavailable or its connectivity check fails.

rules.source_quote: If the user belongs to multiple workspaces, present the list and ask which one to use.
rules.outcome: When the user belongs to more than one workspace, the answer lists them and asks which to use instead of choosing one silently.
rules.why: Planning in the wrong workspace puts tasks where the team will never see them.
rules.scenario_hint: User account belongs to several workspaces and asks to start sprint planning.

rules.outcome: Before planning, the answer confirms the sprint length, points per person and the meaning of one point (defaults of two weeks, ten points per person, one point per work day), asks how many people are on the team, then states the resulting total capacity (e.g. 3 people give 30 points).
rules.why: Without agreed parameters and headcount, capacity figures are guesses and the plan may be over- or under-filled.
rules.scenario_hint: User starts a new sprint plan without stating team size or capacity assumptions.

rules.source_quote: Tasks above 5 points should be broken down
rules.outcome: Any task estimated above five points is split into smaller tasks or subtasks rather than being accepted as a single large estimate.
rules.why: Large estimates hide uncertainty and make sprint commitments unreliable.
rules.scenario_hint: Backlog item is estimated at 8 points or more.

rules.source_quote: Only leaf-level tasks (Tasks/Subtasks) should carry story point estimates
rules.outcome: Points are placed only on the lowest-level work items; parent items that have children carry no estimate of their own, so totals are not double counted.
rules.why: Estimating both parents and children inflates the committed total.
rules.scenario_hint: Plan with a parent story broken into subtasks, each needing estimates.

rules.source_quote: If no story point custom field exists on the project, note this to the user and track points locally
rules.outcome: If the project has no numeric field for story points, the answer tells the user and keeps the point totals in the conversation instead of silently dropping the estimates.
rules.why: Estimates would otherwise be lost and capacity tracking would break.
rules.scenario_hint: Project has no field for story points but the user wants sized tasks.

rules.outcome: As tasks are added, the answer warns when planned points near the sprint's capacity (about four-fifths) and gives a clear alert once the capacity is exceeded.
rules.why: Without warnings the team overcommits before noticing.
rules.scenario_hint: Adding tasks that push the sprint total close to or over capacity.

rules.source_quote: Display remaining capacity after each task added
rules.outcome: After each task is added, the answer shows points used, total capacity and points remaining.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to add several tasks to a sprint plan.

rules.source_quote: For tasks sourced from external tickets: include the ticket ID and URL in the Asana task description
rules.outcome: Tasks created from external tickets carry the ticket identifier and link in their description so work can be traced back.
rules.why: Without the reference, tasks become disconnected from their origin.
rules.scenario_hint: Creating tasks from tickets in another tracker.

rules.source_quote: Present the full create plan for batch approval before executing writes.
rules.outcome: The answer presents the full set of tasks to be created for the user's approval before making any changes, rather than creating them first.
rules.why: Bulk writes to a shared tracker are tedious to undo and may not match what the user wanted.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to create multiple sprint tasks.

rules.outcome: Before rolling unfinished work into the next sprint by recreating tasks, the answer lists the tasks and warns that the old activity log, discussion, files, child items, watchers, labels and other custom data will not carry over, and asks for explicit confirmation.
rules.why: The user could lose information irreversibly without realizing the move is a copy.
rules.scenario_hint: User asks to carry incomplete tasks over to the next sprint.

rules.source_quote: If (d) fails, report both the original and new task GIDs to the user so they can reconcile manually
rules.outcome: When closing an old task fails after its replacement was created, the answer gives the user the identifiers of the old and the new task so the duplicate can be fixed by hand; one task's failure does not stop the others.
rules.why: Silent failures leave duplicate open tasks that double count work.
rules.scenario_hint: Rollover where closing a replaced task fails.
